name: Names the exception (NullPointerException / crash) vs only generic null-safety/robustness language
side_a: No deduct when the answer explicitly names the NullPointerException (or an equivalent 'it will throw/crash on null') somewhere — in analysis, recommendation, or code comment. Saying 'prevent potential NullPointerException' is enough.
side_b: Deduct when the answer only talks about adding a null check in generic terms — 'guard against null', 'make the code more robust', 'protect against accidental null assignments' — and never names the NullPointerException or any thrown/crash consequence. Recommending the null-safe fix alone does not satisfy 'discuss the possible NPE'.

name: Answer states no cause for the null at all (pure defensive-programming advice) vs asserts some causal mechanism
side_a: Do not deduct when the answer never offers any explanation of why mPrefix could be null — it only recommends/declines a null guard on general robustness grounds. With no mechanism asserted, there is nothing that can be an 'incorrect alternative mechanism', so this sub-item cannot fire, even if the answer also fails to mention the cloud-service system property.
side_b: Deduct 2 only when the answer actually commits to a causal mechanism for the null (an identifiable reason mPrefix would be null in this code) and that mechanism is false; mere omission of the real cause is not a wrong mechanism and is handled by other items.
